seen_animation: Frames 1-3: a closed book, drawn as a tilted rectangle with short text dashes, sits on the diagonal with a loopy four-finger hand at its lower right edge; a grey paper outline is behind it at top left. Frame 4: a second offset rectangle outline appears over the book and the hand moves up onto the cover. Frames 5-6: the cover narrows to a thin strip along the upper-left edge and the hand slides up along it. Frame 7: the book is now drawn open, a left page with dashes and a double spine line, with the hand at the left page's top edge. Frames 8-9: the hand moves to the upper left and leaves frame. Frames 10-16: the open book holds still with no hand.
seen_film: Frames 1-4: a hand with red nails rests on the lower right of a black closed binder labelled Federal Reserve Regulations. Frames 5-6: the hand lifts the cover, which swings up to the right and over toward the left with motion blur, exposing printed pages. Frames 7-8: the cover and a block of pages stand up on the left side while the hand pushes them over. Frames 9-10: the hand leaves at the upper left and the lifted pages settle against the left. Frames 11-16: the binder lies open with two page stacks and nearly no motion.
named_subject: A book (binder) being opened by a hand, the doodle of an open book with two pages, text dashes and a double spine line.
evidence: e.png 1-4 match f.png 1-4 (hand resting on closed cover, same place lower right). e.png 5-7: the cover is shown as a second full rectangle laid over the first, so the book reads as doubled; in f.png 5-7 the cover is one surface rising on its hinge. e.png 8-10: the cover is squeezed into a thin strip on the upper-left edge while the hand slides up it, roughly in time with f.png 8-10 where the cover swings over. e.png 10->11: the drawing is replaced in one step, the closed rectangle becomes the open two-page book, the left edge moves out past where the book was, the spine line changes position, and the hand jumps from mid-cover to the upper left at a larger size; f.png 10->11 is a continuous pages-falling motion. e.png 13->14->15: the hand shrinks, jumps to the top-left corner, then appears as a small detached fragment at 15 before vanishing at 16; in f.png 13-15 the hand slides out of frame. e.png 16-26 hold the open book, matching f.png 16-26 where the book is nearly static (the film keeps a page settling on the left that the animation does not show). g.png shows the closed outlines (1-7) and open outlines (10-16) as two separate stacked shapes with no in-between drawings joining them.
primary_gap: The cover does not turn as one swinging surface: it appears as a doubled rectangle at frame 5, collapses to a strip, and then the open book is swapped in at frame 11 with no drawings of the cover passing upright over the spine.
closes_when: Frames 5-12 show a single cover outline rotating about one fixed spine line (rising, standing nearly edge-on, then laying down to the left as the left page), with the earlier rectangle disappearing as the cover leaves it and no frame where two full book outlines overlap.
protect: The open book in frames 11-26 keeps the doodle's construction (two pages, short slanted text dashes, double spine line, plain single-weight strokes); the event timing (hand rests 1-4, opening 5-12, hand exits 12-15, hold 16-26) matches the film; the book sits in the same place and diagonal as the film's binder; the hand stays in the same loose looped-finger style.
identity_gap: The open book matches c.png's two pages, text dashes and double spine, but the closed-book state and the left page's curved outer edge are drawn more loosely than the doodle's near-rectangular pages, so frames 1-10 read only partly as the same drawing.
